subject: Approval request: Early-termination & downgrade protections for Horizon Health pilot
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Horizon pilot: proposed terms and early-termination wording

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. As promised, attaching the updated SOW and a short straw-man for the early-termination / downgrades language so your procurement and legal teams have something concrete to react to. High level: we want to support a low-friction pilot while protecting both parties from asymmetric downside.

Key asks we included in the draft attached (Horizon_SOW_v2.pdf):
- 45-day opt-out during the initial 120-day ramp period (customer can elect to cancel with 45 days' notice)
- Credit mechanism: pro-rated credit for unused committed capacity during remaining term, capped at 100k USD
- A one-time onboarding credit tied to MAP milestones

Commercial: proposing a 30% first-year usage discount for the pilot cohort (non-standard; need exec approval).

Could you share procurement/ legal's preferred opt-out window and whether the credit cap is a blocker? If we need to escalate for exec sign-off, I’ll loop our finance and legal leads.

Appreciate a quick turn — Olivia, if you can confirm your team's timing for redlines that would help.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Horizon_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf)]
From: Olivia Chen <olivia@horizonhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Manager <procure@horizonhealth.com>, Horizon Health Legal <legal@horizonhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Horizon pilot: proposed terms and early-termination wording

Marissa —

Thanks for the draft. Procurement & legal looked it over quickly and a couple of items they flagged:

- 45 days feels long for the pilot. We need a 30-day opt-out window within the first 90 days of the pilot so we can de-risk clinical integration fast.
- If we exercise opt-out, we prefer a credit equal to remaining committed fees (pro-rated) to be applied as invoice credits; no cap is preferred, but we understand commercial sensitivity.

Can Redwood offer a compromise (30-day opt-out, 90-day window) or provide a smaller capped credit? If you can run this up the chain and get back to us today that would be great — legal wants to close redlines before end of quarter.

—Olivia
Olivia Chen | Head of Clinical Integrations, Horizon Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 13:30:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Horizon pilot: proposed terms and early-termination wording — escalation for approval

Soojin / Karthik —

Forwarding Horizon's response (below). Procurement is pushing for a 30-day opt-out within the first 90 days and wants no cap on credits. Legal (Laura) is looped for redline.

Proposal from my side to keep the deal live while limiting Redwood exposure:
- 45-day opt-out window starting any time during the first 120 days OR a customer-triggered 30-day opt-out restricted to the first 90 days (i.e., one of the two choices)
- Pro-rated invoice credit limited to 75k USD cap (down from the 100k in our draft)
- Add requirement for MAP with 3 milestones (onboard completion, integration test, production sign-off) to qualify for credits
- Approve a 25% introductory usage discount (we can comp for the remainder if exec wants more)

Can you confirm whether we have latitude to accept the 30-day/90-day ask or whether Finance will require the capped credit? We need exec guidance to finish redlines today. Attached is an updated redline for exec review (SOW_redline_for_exec.pdf).

Thanks —
Marissa
[Attachment: SOW_redline_for_exec.pdf]
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Horizon pilot: proposed terms and early-termination wording — legal redlines

Team —

Quick legal read: we can probably get to a place where Horizon's procurement is comfortable, but recommend the following guardrails to mitigate open-ended liability:

1) Maintain 45-day opt-out as default; allow one limited 30-day opt-out option if the customer requests it during the first 90 days, but attach a non-refundable onboarding fee (to discourage trivial cancellations).
2) Credit calculation: pro-rated unused committed fees, capped. Recommend cap at 100k USD from a pure legal risk perspective. If finance wants a smaller cap, that's commercial.
3) Limit to one opt-out event per 12-month renewal cycle.
4) Require MAP completion trigger language for eligibility of credits; require notification and a 10-business-day cure period for disputes.

Attached are line edits (legal_comments.docx). Also flag: any cap > 50k requires a finance sign-off (internal policy).

-Laura
Laura Bennett | Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: legal_comments.docx]
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Dec 2026 09:00:00 -0800
Subject: Exec approval request — Horizon Health pilot: downgrades/termination safeguards

Vivek —

Brief: Horizon (large regional health system) is asking for a shorter opt-out (30 days within first 90) and unlimited credit on opt-out. We can say yes with guardrails; legal suggests a 45-day default + optional single 30-day with onboarding fee. Legal also flagged that caps >50k need finance approval.

My recommendation to protect revenue predictability while keeping the customer in the funnel:
- Approve a 45-day opt-out window during the first 120 days OR allow a one-time 30-day opt-out within the first 90 days if Horizon pays a non-refundable onboarding fee of $15k.
- Cap pro-rated credits at $75k (finance-positive compromise vs legal's 100k).
- Approve a 25% introductory usage discount for the pilot (Marissa asked 30%; we can split the difference).
- Require MAP with three milestones; credits only trigger if MAP milestones are met (protects us from immediate cancel after sign-up).

Rationale: preserves close probability, reduces churn risk, limits financial exposure. If you approve, I will instruct Marissa to finalize redline with legal and present to Horizon procurement.

Thanks —
Soojin Lee | VP Sales, Enterprise Accounts
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Dec 2026 14:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exec approval request — Horizon Health pilot: downgrades/termination safeguards

Soojin / team —

Approve the compromise with the following binding conditions:
1) Approve 45-day opt-out OR one-time 30-day opt-out within the first 90 days if customer pays a non-refundable $15k onboarding fee.
2) Cap pro-rated invoice credits at $75k USD.
3) Apply a 25% usage discount for the pilot (final pricing to be reflected in SOW).
4) Credits to be applied as a one-time invoice credit on the next billing cycle following confirmed opt-out.
5) Require signed MAP (three milestones) before credits are eligible; legal to finalize the exact trigger language.

Please update the SOW with these terms and run final doc through legal for the precise clauses. Once legal signs off, Marissa can send to Horizon and we should ask for countersign by EOW to meet quarter close.

Thanks —
Vivek Kulkarni | Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
